title.zh: Bosch-Hale 麦克斯韦聚变反应率

summary: Evaluate the Bosch-Hale fitted Maxwellian reactivity for DT, D-He3 and the two D-D branches without silently clipping ion temperature.

identity.relation: Ion temperature and reaction channel to Maxwellian-averaged fusion reactivity
identity.definition: For channel coefficients BG, MRC2 and C1..C7: theta = T/[1-T(C2+T(C4+TC6))/(1+T(C3+T(C5+TC7)))], xi = (BG^2/(4 theta))^(1/3), <sigma v> = C1 theta sqrt(xi/(MRC2 T^3)) exp(-3 xi) 1e-6. Coefficients are fixed per reaction in the implementation.
identity.model: Bosch-Hale analytical fit for Maxwellian thermal ion reactions; no non-Maxwellian enhancement
identity.geometry: Local scalar relation evaluated elementwise; no plasma geometry
identity.coordinates: Ion temperature in keV and four explicit reaction labels
identity.boundary: No implicit temperature clipping; positive finite inputs are accepted only where the fitted result is finite and representable.
assumptions: The supplied temperature is the ion temperature for a Maxwellian reaction-rate model.
Reactant densities, fuel composition and fusion power are separate relations.

inputs.name: ion_temperature_kev
inputs.shape: scalar or any nonempty array shape
inputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive; booleans, strings, complex values and empty arrays are rejected.

inputs.name: reaction
inputs.constraints: Exactly DT, DHe3, DD_Tp or DD_He3n.

outputs.name: reactivity
outputs.shape: float for scalar input, otherwise same shape as ion_temperature_kev
outputs.constraints: Finite for accepted input; zero may result from floating-point underflow at low temperature.

preconditions: The caller selects the appropriate reaction branch and supplies an ion temperature in keV.
The Bosch-Hale Maxwellian fit is the intended model; independent physical validity for every accepted temperature is not established.
supported: Four named light-ion reaction channels with ASCOT5 coefficient precision.
Scalar and nonempty array evaluation with shape preservation and no input mutation.
excluded: Fusion cross section as a function of projectile energy and reaction-product kinematics.
TokaGrad's rounded DT coefficients, silent 0.2-200 keV clipping, fuel composition, power-density and fast-ion partition semantics.
Claims of fit accuracy outside an independently established scientific domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for an unknown channel or nonnumeric, boolean, complex, empty, nonfinite or nonpositive temperature.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError when the fitted theta is nonpositive/nonfinite or the output is nonfinite; other unexpected NumPy errors propagate.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; this is not an iterative solve.
failure_semantics.partial_results: None; all elements must pass validation before output is returned.

provenance.lineage_summary: The standard four-channel fit uses the saved ASCOT5 boschhale reaction-rate coefficients. TokaGrad supplies a DT-only implementation of the same algebraic relation with rounded coefficients and 0.2-200 keV clipping; it is overlapping evidence, not exact implementation reuse. Independent whole-source review later withdrew both projects' former strict D1 qualification. Their archived candidate trees and bounded numerical comparisons remain historical development evidence, not current qualified L1 input; exact references and limits are in the 2026-09-25 extraction handoff and intake evaluation.
source_kinds: archived ASCOT5 and TokaGrad L1 operator contracts and implementations, pending renewed strict D1 review
saved ASCOT5 compiled-source golden and direct L1 tests
saved TokaGrad source-free equation tests and bounded numerical comparison
public_references: Bosch and Hale, Nuclear Fusion 32 (1992), doi:10.1088/0029-5515/32/4/I07

example.description: Evaluate DT Maxwellian reactivity at 10 keV.
example.code:
from scirel.fusion import evaluate_bosch_hale_reactivity
rate = evaluate_bosch_hale_reactivity(10.0, reaction='DT')
assert abs(rate / 1.1361654705836232e-22 - 1) < 1e-11
example.expected: DT <sigma v> is approximately 1.1361654705836232e-22 m^3/s at 10 keV.

scope: Four channel source-golden values, positive real scalar and array behavior, input validation and no clipping.
Pinned ASCOT5 and TokaGrad saved implementations compared on finite temperatures; rounded DT discrepancy and clipping distinguished.
verification.evidence_ceiling: ASCOT5's saved direct test reports compiled-source parity and historical SciRel replay checks the saved implementation at listed temperatures. TokaGrad's saved test is source-free only; its DT values differ by up to about 4.6e-5 relative on sampled 0.2-200 keV inputs. Both project-level strict D1 qualifications were withdrawn; neither comparison proves a current qualified source package, physical fit validity for all temperatures, complete source-project reproduction or expert approval.
known_limitations: No reaction cross section, product kinematics, fuel density or fusion power is exposed.
No caller-specific temperature clipping or profile policy is inferred.
TokaGrad's negative-density validation claim conflicts with its saved implementation and is not adopted.
Distribution license and expert science approval remain pending.
